source.title: Soft Matching Distance: A metric on neural representations that captures single-neuron tuning

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether activation tuning is reproducible across independently trained networks using soft-matching similarity and a rotation sweep, rather than the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative results for alignment across seeds, architectures, and datasets as a function of basis rotation (Fig. 4B-D), plus comparisons showing that similarity judgments differ by metric (Fig. 3A-B). The NSD model-to-brain comparisons are recorded as related findings but do not test convergence between independently trained models. The paper's discussion of alternative metrics and cited prior findings is not treated as new empirical evidence.
record.test_reason: Uses a new rotation-sensitive soft-matching score and a basis-rotation sweep to test whether separately trained CNNs share unit-level tuning bases. It compares networks across seeds (V3), and across architectures and datasets (unit-level recurrence, V5). It does not use the original studies' methods.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that soft matching shows activation bases converge above chance across seeds, architectures and datasets, supporting 'tuning matters' over 'geometry is all you need'. They also conclude it complements rotation-invariant metrics and discriminates model-brain fits better than linear predictivity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a rotation-sensitive soft-matching correlation/distance based on optimal transport and a gradual basis-rotation analysis; it does not reproduce the original methods. The paper is a research paper proposing and applying a metric.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent alignment depends on basis rotation and on the similarity metric: rotation-invariant measures miss the distinction captured by soft matching. The toy example also gives different similarity assessments under semi-matching and soft matching.

fits_no_version.finding: Rotation-invariant measures (Procrustes, CKA, CCA) treat a layer and its random rotation as identical, whereas soft matching separates them. In toy examples, semi-matching yields intransitive similarity judgments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rotation-invariant similarity measures cannot detect whether unit-level tuning is shared, so convergence measured with them concerns geometry only.

fits_no_version.finding: Soft-matching model-to-fMRI similarity separates CNNs from ViTs and the ventral stream from the dorsal and lateral streams, while linear predictivity ranks all model-region pairs similarly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-brain alignment conclusions depend on the metric's invariance class.

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; the text says under review
record.problems: The convergence results are qualitative in the text and presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments are limited to image-network settings and do not test scale or capability.

untested.parts: No variation in model size or capability. Cross-architecture results (R3-R4) do not test whether alignment grows with scale.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparisons.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired alignment tests.
Does not show that the shared units are interpretable features or circuits. The authors note most hidden units are not semantically meaningful. No SAE features.

No empirical comparison of convergence between trained models under different metrics, neighbour settings or OOD inputs. Metric differences are shown only on self-rotations, toy examples and model-brain comparisons.
No plateau analysis and no test of shared data or objectives as causes.
Shared subspaces are not measured separately, and no numerical scores are given.

missing.what: Numerical soft-matching scores, chance (random-basis) levels and uncertainty for the seed, architecture and dataset comparisons

record.verdict_notes: All model-model results are qualitative and figure-only, from small CIFAR CNNs. The V3 finding is consistent with 'not identical' units but suggests bases are less arbitrary than a pure shared-subspace reading implies. The V6 labels from the record were dropped because no metric-dependence result concerns convergence between trained models.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability; no test that alignment rises with scale or performance.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language models.
Measures similarity of tuning curves/bases, not shared feature identities or shared subspaces as separate quantities; no test of whether individual units or bases are identical.
No mapping between representations, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

Tests differences between rotation-sensitive and rotation-invariant metrics, but not neighbour-count settings, out-of-distribution inputs, or a broad sweep of datasets and similarity measures on convergence results.
Does not test a convergence plateau or whether shared data/objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality.
